definition.body: Falsetto voice is a classification category for a mode of phonation defined by a specific glottal configuration: the vocal folds are stretched and thinned, with only the superficial layer of the fold vibrating in a high-register cycle at a fundamental frequency above the modal range, under reduced subglottal pressure, producing the soft, reedy, thin timbre of the falsetto mode. Its parameters are: (1) the glottal configuration - stretched, thin fold with superficial-layer vibration and reduced subglottal pressure, (2) the cycle signature - high f0 above the speaker's modal range with reduced-cycle-amplitude periodic vibration of the thin membrane, (3) the acoustic signature - a soft, reedy timbre with a weak high-harmonic structure. It persists as a named mode of the phonation-mode taxonomy: documented in laryngology and phonetics, used in voice-disorder assessment (falsetto as a thin, reedy voice quality) and in voice training (the falsetto contrasted with the modal mode), and maintained alongside the other voice modes. e.g.: the falsetto mode in Sundberg's 1987 phonation inventory (The Science of the Singing Voice); the 'falsetto voice' category on a voice therapy plan for a speaker with a habitually thin, reedy high voice; the falsetto label in a phonetic description of a singer's high head register | not: the operatic falsetto repertoire of a countertenor (a performance-practice register, not the laryngeal mode); modal phonation (complete closure at modal frequency); whisper voice (unvoiced glottal airflow, outside voiced phonation) [formal: vox falsa | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes]

definition.body: Whisper voice is a classification category for aperiodic phonation defined by a specific glottal configuration: the vocal folds are abducted and held apart without glottal contact, so that no periodic vibration is produced; sound is generated instead by turbulent airflow noise through the open glottis. Its parameters are: (1) the glottal configuration - abducted folds, no glottal contact, no periodic vibration of the folds, (2) the sound-generation mechanism - broadband turbulent noise of the airflow through the open glottis, without a harmonic stack, (3) the acoustic signature - a noise-like sound with no stable fundamental frequency, often with vocal-tract formant structure. It persists as a named mode of the phonation-mode taxonomy: documented in laryngology and phonetics, used in voice therapy (whisper voice as the voice-rest technique after laryngeal surgery), and maintained alongside modal, falsetto, and creaky phonation. e.g.: the whisper-voice category on a post-laryngoscopy voice-rest plan; the whisper-voice label in a phonetic description of a child's whispered speech; the whisper-voice category in the phonation-mode inventory maintained in laryngology | not: falsetto voice (periodic high-f0 vibration of the thin membrane, still voiced); creaky voice (periodic low-frequency vibration with glottal contact); modal voice (complete glottal closure at modal frequency) [formal: vox susurrata | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes]

definition.body: Pressed voice (hyperfunctional phonation) is a classification category for a mode of phonation defined by a specific glottal configuration: the vocal folds are adducted with heavy medial contact under elevated subglottal pressure, vibrating with a short open phase and a long closed phase relative to the modal cycle, producing a tight, strained, rough timbre with elevated pitch. payload.name: area-quotient
payload.scope: A human-made measurement construct that quantifies the fraction of the glottal cycle occupied by a specific phase of vocal fold contact or openness, computed as a ratio of time intervals within the fundamental period, built to persist as the foundational quotient family for quantifying glottal geometry in speech science and laryngology.

definition.body: The area quotient is a voice-quality measurement construct quantifying the fraction of the glottal cycle during which the glottal aperture is in a specified state (open, closed, or transitioning), computed as the ratio of the duration of that state to the fundamental period. From the time-varying glottal area function A(t) within a single glottal cycle of period T0, the area quotient is Q = t_state / T0 where t_state is the total time during which A(t) satisfies a specified threshold condition. Its parameters are: (1) the glottal area function A(t) over the cycle, (2) the threshold defining the state boundary (e.g., A(t) > ε for open, A(t) ≤ ε for closed), (3) the fundamental period T0 from pitch tracking. The open quotient (A(t) > threshold), closed quotient (A(t) ≤ threshold), and area-moment quotients are all specific instantiations of this general construct. It persists as a standardized measurement in speech science and clinical laryngology, computed by glottal analysis software (Praat with glottal analysis extensions, KSE, glotfit) from glottal-flow-derived area functions. e.g.: the open quotient parameter in Sundberg's voice analysis protocol; the closed quotient computed from the area-velocity model in the KSE software toolkit; the area-moment quotient used in laryngoscopy-based glottal cycle analysis | not: contact-quotient [formal: quotiens arealis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes]

payload.name: speech-signal
payload.scope: A human-made construct of the acoustic waveform produced by the speech production apparatus, built to persist as the primary analysis signal in speech science — the physical medium from which voice quality, prosody, and articulatory parameters are extracted through signal processing.

definition.body: The speech signal is the acoustic waveform generated by the speech production system, consisting of the pressure variations radiated from the mouth and nose over time. It is the output of the source-filter process: the glottal flow waveform g(n) filtered by the vocal tract transfer function H(f). Its parameters are: (1) the temporal pressure waveform p(t) or its discrete samples p[n], (2) the sampling rate and bit depth defining its digital representation, (3) the framing parameters (window length, hop size) used in analysis. It persists as a standardized signal construct in speech science and engineering, captured by microphones, represented in audio file formats (WAV, FLAC), and analyzed in signal processing toolkits (Praat, Librosa, Kaldi). e.g.: the WAV file of a sustained /a/ vowel recorded at 44.1 kHz for acoustic analysis; the framed speech signal used in the Kaldi speech recognition toolkit for feature extraction; the recorded speech waveform in the TIMIT speech corpus for phonetic research | not: glottal flow (the subglottal-side airflow waveform, before vocal tract filtering); vocal tract resonance (the filtered output after glottal flow passes through the vocal tract) [formal: vox sermo | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes]

payload.name: perturbation
payload.scope: A human-made measurement construct quantifying the cycle-to-cycle variation of a periodic parameter in voiced speech — the deviation from regularity that distinguishes stable phonation from dysphonic or irregular phonation — built to persist as a standardized classification of voice instability in speech science and laryngology.

definition.body: Perturbation is a voice-quality measurement construct quantifying the cycle-to-cycle variation (deviation from regularity) of a periodic parameter in voiced speech. Given N consecutive cycles of a parameter with values v_i, perturbation is computed as a normalized measure of dispersion: typically the standard deviation of the per-cycle values divided by their mean, expressed as a percentage or absolute value. Its parameters are: (1) the periodic parameter being measured (fundamental period for jitter/period perturbation, amplitude for shimmer/amplitude perturbation, HNR harmonic amplitude for shimmer of harmonics), (2) the perturbation variant (APQ — average absolute difference, JRR — jitter ratio, JDP — jitter difference), (3) the number of cycles N. It persists as a standardized clinical voice-quality parameter, computed by acoustic analysis software (Praat, MDVP, laryngology toolkits) from pitch-synchronous period tracks or amplitude envelopes. e.g.: the jitter (APQ1) value reported in a standard voice assessment per GRBAS protocol; the shimmer (APQ5) computed by the MDVP voice analysis module in the 3500 Bio-logic system; the JRR (jitter-ratio) value in a laryngology report documenting dysphonia severity | not: noise-to-harmonics ratio (measures signal-to-noise ratio, not cycle-to-cycle variation of a periodic parameter); glottal-flow derivative (a time-domain waveform feature, not a perturbation measure) [formal: perturbatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes]
